function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repository.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Docker image for the Node.js app |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow that builds & pushes the image on every push to `main` |

> **NOTE** – The repo is assumed to be cloned locally (`git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`).  
> After you copy the files into the repo, run the usual `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` commands.

---

## 1. Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image: Node.js 18 (Alpine) – small footprint
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set maintainer
LABEL maintainer="Unknown"

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "index.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * The repo is a simple Node.js app (see `index.js` and `package.json`).  
> * Using `node:18-alpine` keeps the image small.  
> * `npm ci --only=production` installs only production deps, speeding up builds.  
> * The app listens on port **3000** (the default for many Node/Express examples).  
> * The entrypoint `node index.js` matches the repo’s start script.

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML

Create a folder `k8s/` (or any name you prefer) and add `deployment.yaml`:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
  labels:
    app: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nodejs-welcome
          image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change if you use another registry
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          env:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80          # Service port
      targetPort: 3000  # Container port
  type: ClusterIP
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys 2 replicas of the container.  
> * Exposes the app on port 80 inside the cluster (via the Service).  
> * Uses `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest` as the image – adjust to your registry if needed.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the file `.github/workflows/build.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/build.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR)
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} \
            .

      # Push the image to GHCR
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

> **How it works**  
> 1. Triggered on every push to `main`.  
> 2. Checks out the repo.  
> 3. Logs into GHCR using the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.  
> 4. Builds two tags: `latest` and the commit SHA.  
> 5. Pushes both tags to GHCR.  

> **Prerequisites**  
> * The repo must be under an organization or user that has permission to push to `ghcr.io`.  
> * No extra secrets are required because `GITHUB_TOKEN` is automatically provided.

---

## 4. Add, Commit & Push

```bash
# From the root of the cloned repo
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run, build the image, and push it to GHCR.  
> You can then deploy to Kubernetes using:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

---

### Quick Recap

| Step | Command |
|------|---------|
| Clone repo | `git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git` |
| Add files | `git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml` |
| Commit | `git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"` |
| Push | `git push origin main` |

That’s it! Your repo now has a production‑ready Dockerfile, Kubernetes deployment/service, and a CI pipeline that automatically builds & publishes the image whenever you push to `main`. Happy coding!
